entities.summary:
The Liber Memorialis is a pivotal ancient Latin book that encapsulates a remarkably condensed summary of universal history from the earliest times to the reign of Trajan. Written by Lucius Ampelius, a likely tutor or schoolmaster, around 123 AD, this concise index showcases Ampelius' remarkable understanding of the past. The Liber Memorialis not only provides a unique window into the historical imagination of the Roman Empire but also serves as a testament to the enduring power of written records in shaping our understanding of the world. As a cultural artifact, the Liber Memorialis stands as a remarkable example of the intersection of history, literature, and education during the Late Roman period.

The Liber Memorialis is a testament to the significant impact of Lucius Ampelius on the field of ancient history. By compiling a vast array of information into a single, easily digestible narrative, Ampelius created a resource that would be studied and referenced for centuries to come. The book's concise summary of universal history demonstrates Ampelius' remarkable grasp of the subject matter, which was likely influenced by his experience as a tutor or schoolmaster.

The Liber Memorialis has left an indelible mark on the field of ancient history, with its influence still felt today. The book's unique blend of history, literature, and education has made it a cornerstone of the discipline, providing a window into the historical imagination of the Roman Empire and serving as a testament to the enduring power of written records.

The Liber Memorialis is a fascinating example of the cultural and intellectual currents of the Late Roman period. The book's concise summary of universal history provides a unique insight into the historical context of the time, while its use of Latin highlights the linguistic and cultural sophistication of the Roman Empire.
